description:
Word on the street is folx are still talking about Oliver Tree’s appearance at last year’s Boston Calling. But the truth is that folx are usually talking about the genre-bending California musician no matter what stage he takes over, and for us here in Boston, Tree now sets his eclectic sights on MGM Music Hall at Fenway on January 19. He’ll be bringing along a few items, notably new album Alone In A Crowd ,  his new character creation Cornelius Cummings, and punk band FIDLAR for opening responsibilities.
Self-described musician, filmmaker, and belly dancer Oliver Tree has made waves on and off the internet for his eccentricity and fuck ass bobs. The Californian multi-hyphenate — who was one of the most talked-about performers at Boston Calling ’22 — released his third album, Alone in a Crowd , last fall via Atlantic Records, along with its accompanying fashion designer persona in Cornelius Cummings . Now, Tree is taking the show on the road with the aptly titled Alone in a Crowd Tour, which hits MGM Music Hall at Fenway this Friday (January 19). As expected, he has a lot to say about it.
Ahead of the tour kicking off in Chicago a few days ago, Tree jumped on the phone with Vanyaland to discuss what to expect from the mega production of the show, as well as comparing filmmaking to music making, and why he considers the upcoming Boston appearance to be a hometown gig. We sat back and let Tree just let it rip.
(Note: the following interview has been edited for length, flow, and clarity.)
Vanyaland: You’re starting a tour [this past weekend] in Chicago. How are you feeling about that?
Oliver Tree: I’m excited. I’ve been working on the show for five years. So it’s a mixture of a movie, a TV show, a concert, and a Broadway play. There is a 360 entertainment component that also includes stand up comedy, uh, motivational speaking, WWE wrestling, karate scooter tricks, as well as some belly dancing, obviously. The music side is a mixture of alternative pop, rock, hip hop, electronic, dance, folk, a little bit of my attempt at country music. It’s a wide span and array of different styles and I’m really excited about that. That’s one show that I’m doing.
I’m also playing a same another show the same night, where I will be debuting my Doctor Oliver Tree project, which is a DJ set afterparty [ taking place at The Grand in the Seaport]. And I’ve been working on this show for a year and a half. Boston will be the official first look at the audio-visual show I’ve been developing for the last year and a half. Obviously, the focus is the first show, which I’ve been developing for a long time, but this other DJ set is something I poured my heart into. It’s something super next level. It pushes the boundaries on what DJing is and can be. Everything is hyper edited and remixed and my fingertips are covering every millisecond of every moment. It’s a mixture of my music, mixed with all my favorite nostalgic music edited to my exact tastes, with visual components that incorporate some of my work as well as my favorite snippets, fully edited and chopped up beyond oblivion, of my favorite moments in cinema.
It’s very psychedelic, very visceral, very raw. It’s called Doctor Oliver Tree, so I’m really excited about that as well. That’s kind of something that’s a new thing. I haven’t even announced that my fans or anything, but I’m very, very excited about that.
What can folks expect from the two shows?
Well for both of the shows, it’s extremely eclectic. So there will be something for everyone. The main show, the Alone in a Crowd Tour, that is full showmanship, full entertainment meets art meets technology. There is a choose your own adventure aspect where the audience can kind of decide what they want to watch. There’s a lot happening visually on the screen. There’s also a full band, an orchestra, there’s a lot of moving parts to it all. You can kind of latch on to whichever parts you want. That’s for people that are kind of not really aware of what they’re getting themselves into.
People who are a fan of [the music], they can expect the best of from the first album, Ugly is Beautiful , mixed with the best stuff of the second album, Cowboy Tears , mixed with the best of Alone in a Crowd . It kind of combines all these worlds, and you get a chance to be introduced to the different characters and personas and see how the whole world and “Oliverse,” the Oliver Tree multiverse, comes together. You get a sense of how the dots are all connected and it covers a lot of the heart and soul put into the music. But there’s a lot of tongue-in-cheek and satire and parody and the visual component as well as some pretty heavy statements on commercialism and exploring a wide plethora of all things meta.
Essentially the crowd is watching me on stage while I perform, as well as at times, [I’m] sitting on a couch, my character’s on a screen in their house, watching themselves on a screen, watching them in their own music videos, which in some music videos they’re even watching themselves again. So it’s five layers deep at times.
Not a lot of people know this, but I lived in Boston until I was six years old, south of Boston. And I go back every summer, so this will be essentially a hometown show for me. I’ve been touring for almost a year now, and it’s very well oiled, and I’ve kind of got it down to math and science. So I’m very excited to bring it back to the motherland, pushing forward both these sets, [including the DJ set] that I’m debuting in Boston as well as the live show before that.
They’re both on the cusp of pushing forward the idea of what these kinds of performances can be. Not that you can ever recreate wheel, but I think that there are some pretty big ideas being contributed here. I’m not saying I’ve invented anything, but I’m very excited to be contributing some new ideas in the creative space.
How does filmmaking compare to music for you?
Ultimately I consider them probably as far apart, creatively speaking, as they can be while still being a form of art that is released digitally online. Music is a little more improv-based. I was just in Hong Kong and I was in hotel rooms, recording, just improvising, making it by myself. Just the raw thing. And when you get to film, it’s the exact opposite. It’s pretty much an army of people. Some of these videos had hundreds of people helping create them, so full collaboration, very rigid planning. Everything’s planned down to the millisecond
They’re very much wildly different. Music is very much so instantaneous. I think that’s why I ultimately chose it as my main medium, because it’s a lot easier to get someone to invest even ten seconds to listen. They’ll know if they like it or not within the first 10 or 30 seconds. It’s pretty hard to get someone to watch a film. Even a music video is a little harder to than a song to get someone to, sit down and watch. But in the same breath, filmmaking to me is like the greatest art form in a sense, because it’s all art forms combined. You mix together everything I’ve ever done as a human, like, for example, the writing, the production, direction, acting, the stunts (cause I have a background as a professional scooter rider and doing action sports), choreography, designing costumes. There’s so much in there that for me, I feel like it’s a way where I can kind of put a lot of my own self into it, whereas music, you have a little bit less room for that.
Going back to the evolution of your sound over the course of three albums, you went more country-adjacent on your second album [ Cowboy Tears ], and then this latest release is a sonic departure from that. What has that process been like for you over the course of these album cycles?
I make art for myself first and foremost when I’m creating. I need to be able to reinvent myself and feel inspired, and the goal of creating the Oliver Tree project was to never be pigeonholed as one thing. So I’ve always kind of kept my audience on their toes. And not every single thing is made for every single person, but there is something for everyone.
After spending five or six years doing the first rollout of Ugly is Beautiful , it was so, so dense. It was like 20 videos of the same character. I was just so ready for something so wildly different, and the exact last thing anyone would expect [would be] to make a country album, because I don’t even like country music. So I had fun with that, as well as getting in touch with my roots. It wasn’t like it was un-authentic because my grandfather was a cowboy. I grew up to the ranch, working on the ranch. His father was a cowboy. His father before that was a cowboy, so it’s part of my lineage. And as I was looking internally at what I wanted to do, that kind of made sense [in addition to] the time I spent on the ranch during COVID.
I had set some rigid rules on what the album sonically should be. No rapping, everything needed to have basically acoustic guitar. There were a lot of rigid rules and it was more of a concept album. And that’s kind of one of those things [where if] people aren’t into that sound for one of the songs, then they’re probably not as likely to like any of it.
That being said, I wasn’t worried about that. I wasn’t trying to make some commercial thing. I was coming off of the success of “Life Goes On,” which was the first song that became a big TikTok song for me. So I didn’t really need to have the commercial success. That was truly artistic expression, a statement on macho, being able to kind of say it’s okay for guys and not just guys, but for everyone to cry. It’s important to cry, we can let out our aggression or sadness through the tears instead of through violence. So I think it was a cool concept.
The third album was coming off the tail of “Miss You” and the success of that, which was my second big TikTok song. The more more famous I became, for lack of a better term — I hate the idea of celebrity, I hate idea of fame, but it’s part of the job as far as getting my art to be heard and seen by people — I felt more lonely than ever.
I had amassed 50 million TikTok followers, but I [had] never felt so lonely. And that story is not exactly that relatable, nor is it particularly that interesting. But more importantly, to create art that connects with people, there has to be a relatability factor. So what’s more relatable than being lonely? It didn’t matter the reasons behind it. So I wanted to make an album that celebrated learning to be able to be alone and to recognize that everybody’s lonely at some point or another. We’re all dealing with loneliness. It’s part of the human experience. And if you look around, you see all these lonely people, it actually makes the experience a little bit less lonely. So I made that the core messaging.
And in the process of it, I made maybe seven or eight versions of the same album, and it was a lot darker at first. After coming out of Cowboy Tears and making a breakup album that was already somewhat dark and a little depressing, I had started falling in love during the process of Alone in a Crowd . I feel like I always forget to document the falling in love process. So I wanted to capsulate it and put it into a bottle and be able to share it with other people. I still think that it can apply to the concept. You can still be alone in a crowd with someone else. Ultimately the goal is to take people out of their darkness and bring some color into their life — make them feel a little bit better about what they’re dealing with.
header: Oliver Tree , Alone In A Crowd, January 19

description: From Kalamazoo to the world! Greensky Bluegrass may have kicked off their Fall Tour last night in Nevada, but time marches on, and the bluegrass jam quintet are already mapping out their famed Winter Tour. The details hit this week, and part of the 24-date trek across the eastern half of North America is a February 2 romp at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway . Earlier this year, the band released a pair of tracks, “Get Out” and “Congratulations & Condolences,” both of which are b-sides from the Michigan band’s 2022 album Stress Dreams . Give “Get Out” a spin below. Mandolin player and vocalist Paul Hoffman sets it up: “‘Get Out’ is anchored in internal reflection but also includes commentary on our society’s struggle to better itself.
header: Greensky Bluegrass , Winter Tour, February 2

description:
One of the more notable aspects of Mitski’s ever-expanding North American tour is the artist performing multiple nights at each venue, like four shows next week at New York’s Beacon Theatre, and four shows in April at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville. Boston gets its own quartet of shows, and they start tonight and run through Saturday (February 15 to 18) at MGM Music Hall at Fenway .
The acclaimed American singer and songwriter is on the road supporting her enchanting and stripped-down 2023 album The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We , which she describes as her “most American album.” It’s the follow-up to 2022 full-length Laurel Hell .
The multi-night stints in cities, Mitski says, is by design. “Ticket-buying is incredibly difficult these days, and I truly appreciate what you all go through to come to our concerts,” she wrote on Instagram last fall. “In our efforts to make the show experience extra special, we found beautiful, seated theaters to play over multiple nights, rather than one giant venue per city, in the hopes of offering a more intimate experience to the audience.”
header: MITSKI + TAMINO :: Thursday, February 15 to Saturday, February 18 at MGM Music Hall, 2 Lansdowne St. in Boston, MA :: $36.50 to $86.50 :: Event info and tickets

description: The world is a very ugly place, so sometimes — well, a lot of times — we need to be reminded of the beauty around us. Chelsea Cutler is doing her part in early 2024, unveiling the 29-date The Beauty Is Everywhere Tour that plays MGM Music Hall at Fenway on February 24. The tour is in support of the Connecticut singer-songwriter’s new album Stellaria . “Making this album has been unequivocally the most difficult creative process I have experienced,” Cutler says. “But this album gave me a chance to experience every emotion on the spectrum. It forced me to confront questions I had previously been too afraid to ask myself, both professionally and personally. It challenged me to push myself again and again to be better than last time. It offered me moments of intense creative and collaborative joy.
header: Chelsea Cutler , The Beauty Is Everywhere Tour, February 24

description: In the world of Subtronics , the bass is relentless, and there’s something for everyone. So while the Philadelphia dubstep DJ and producer born Jesse Kardon has been hella productive lately — new album ANTIFRACTALS hit at the end of 2022; bass juggernaut Excision collab “Asteroid” just shook up the streams — we’re perhaps most shaken by his drum & bass remix of Phantogram’s modern classic “Black Out Days.” All of that and more should be on full kaledioscopic display as Subtronics delivers the TESSERACT Tour to MGM Music Hall at Fenway for two nights, March 2 and 3. “Drawing inspiration from the ‘tesseract’, a geometric marvel known in fourth-dimensional geometry as a 16-cell cube, Subtronics (who has a tattoo of a tesseract on his arm) channeled his fascination into an innovative stage design accompanied by breathtaking visual elements,” states the pitch. The full-slate evenings also feature Wooli, Hedex, Saka, Jon Casey, Skellytn, SuperAve., and Automhate.
header: Subtronics , TESSERACT Tour, March 2 and 3

description: March in Boston is usually one big party, and one weekend in particular will boast two Saturday nights. California rapper and singer-songwriter Bryce Vine brings his Saturday Night Tour to town for a Sunday, March 10 romp at MGM Music Hall at Fenway , extending the weekend and enhancing our vibes. The “Margot Robbie” artist is bringing Hoodie Allen and Yoshi T along for the ride, and if his Myspace-inspired homepage is any indication, it should be a good time.
header: Bryce Vine , The Saturday Night Tour, March 10

description: Never mind the rest of the calendar; Boston’s greatest holiday is still several months away. But St. Patrick’s Day got a little bit closer this week as Dropkick Murphys unveiled their annual residency on Lansdowne Street. The Celtic punk band’s 2024 swing includes an opening show at House of Blues on March 14, then a trio of shows at MGM Music Hall at Fenway from March 15 to 17. Pennywise will support each show, and additional opening acts announced in the coming months. As we reported earlier in the week, the Dropkicks news arrives in the midst of the band’s current U.S. tour. In addition to this year’s prior St. Patrick’s Day shows, Dropkick Murphys also performed at Boston Calling this May as a last-minute substitute for the Yeah Yeah Yeahs, who dropped off the lineup one day before they were scheduled to perform.
header: Dropkick Murphys , St. Patrick’s Day shows, March 15 to 17

description: Are we ready for some “Bass to the Dome”? Well, we have until March 24 to prepare both physically and mentally, as Excision brings the Nexus Tour to MGM Music Hall at Fenway . The DJ/producer from Kelowna, British Columbia brings his bass thunder to Boston, part of a massive 2024 tour: “It’s the largest tour we’ve done with 50-plus dates, massive production and heavy support lineups the whole way,” Excision writes. Here’s the word from Insomniac: “Excision shows are like no other. A virtual apocalypse of twisting and morphing sounds turn massive crowds into a frenzy. Earth-shattering walls of bass relentlessly smash upon the bodies of headbanging fans around the world.” Buckle up.
header: Excision , Nexus Tour, March 24

description: Norwegian alt-pop mainstay girl in red is prepping her “biggest show to you ever” , and it all starts here in Boston. The singer-songwriter and producer born Marie Ulven has announced her Doing It Again World Tour, named for forthcoming new album I’M DOING IT AGAIN BABY! , and the North American leg kicks off with an April 16 twirl at MGM Music Hall at Fenway , just four days after the record drops. Making it all the more exciting is that Vanyaland faves Momma are on board as direct support. Last week, girl in red shared the album’s lead single, a vibrant indie bop called “Too Much.” Ulven has this to say about it: “I’ve always been told I’m ‘Too Much’. Throughout my whole childhood and in my adult years. Getting shut down when I’m at my happiest or most excited made me feel self-conscious, alienated, and weird… It wasn’t until I encountered the same feeling in my relationships, that I realized how much it actually hurt me to never feel fully accepted for who I am.
header: girl in red , Doing It Again World Tour, April 16

description: The Black Crowes are back, and even though life is twice as hard as it was back in the ’90s, the brothers Robinson are sounding pretty reinvigorated. Just take a listen to lethal new single “Wanting And Waiting,” which sounds like classic Crowes at their bluesy, ballsy best. In March, they release Happiness Bastards , the Georgia band’s 10th studio album and first of original music in 15 years. A tour named for the album takes flight right after, hitting Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on April 28. “ Happiness Bastards is our love letter to rock n’ roll,” says Chris Robinson. “Rich and I are always writing and creating music; that has never stopped for us, and it is always where we find harmony together. This record represents that.” Adds Rich Robinson: “This album is a continuation of our story as a band.
header: The Black Crowes , Happiness Bastards Tour, April 28

description: Springtime in Boston usually means college students are busy prepping for finals. So it makes perfect sense that Professor Greg Graffin will be rolling into town. Graffin’s punk mainstays Bad Religion are teaming up with Lynn-born Mike Ness and Social Distortion for a co-headlining North American tour that hits MGM Music Hall at Fenway on May 7. The run finds Social D playing classic debut album Mommy’s Little Monster for its 40th anniversary, and are the first shows since Ness’ tonsil cancer diagnosis. Says Ness: “Yes, we are back in action and can’t wait for this tour! We did this with [Bad Religion] in Australia in 2022 and the shows were amazing! We have also decided in celebration of the 40-year anniversary and re-release of Mommy’s Little Monster that we will be playing the album in its entirety. This should be a very special tour and we are all looking forward to it.” Adds Graffin: “Bad Religion and Social Distortion played together in 1980. Though we evolved in different directions, we both carried the torch of Southern California punk all along the way.
header: Bad Religion and Social Distortion , May 7

description: As we slowly begin to enter a new year, the Silence Between Songs grows louder and louder, as Madison Beer is set to take her sophomore album out on the road for 52 dates in 2024. One of those dates is marked for Boston, as Beer brings The Spinnin Tour to MGM Music Hall at Fenway on May 11. The tour is named after the album’s opening track and enigmatic alt-pop single, which has already racked up more than 10 million streams across multiple platforms. “This song is a reflection of a time when everything seemed to stand still,” says Beer. “I felt like every day was a cycle and I was stuck in such an anxious place, yet I could finally explore the thoughts and emotions in my head.
header: Madison Beer , The Spinnin Tour, May 11

description: Every now and then we must travel “One Step Beyond” the confines of “Our House,” and theres no better way to know “It Must Be Love” than seeing Madness on their first North American tour in a dozen years. The legendary English ska/pop band have announced a handful of stateside dates around an appearance at Las Vegas’ Punk Rock Bowling, and included is a May 29 dance party at MGM Music Hall at Fenway . Last November, Madness released their eighth album, Theatre of the Absurd Presents C’est la Vie . “I remember the first time we were in the  USA, crossing the Brooklyn Bridge, The Mud Club, ABC City,” says Madness frontman Suggs in a press release. “I remember Jelly Bean Benetiz, Madonna, Beastie Boys, Run DC Link Ray. I remember California, Fishbone, BossTones, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Whisky Gogo, The Dead Kennedys.
header: Madness , C’est La Vie In America, May 29

description: Get ready for a whole lot of Gary Clark Jr. in 2024. The Austin blues guitarist and singer is set to release new album JPEG RAW in March, and has already unveiled a four-song sampler platter to set the mood. Next month, Clark performs live on NBC’s The Tonight Show , and in the spring kicks off a United States tour in support of the record. Included in the itinerary are appearances at Red Rocks Amphitheatre, Radio City Music Hall, and Bonnaroo, as well as a local stop at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on June 7. JPEG RAW is the awaited follow-up to 2019’s This Land , and it features collaborations with Stevie Wonder and George Clinton. In the time since his last record, Clark also played Arthur “Big Boy” Crudup in Baz Luhrmann’s 2022 biopic Elvis .
header: Gary Clark Jr. , June 7

description: From humble New Jersey beginnings to bands like Fun and Steel Train to Grammy-winning production work for the likes of Taylor Swift and Florence and the Machine, Jack Antonoff has been a force in pop music for over a decade. Now, his alt-pop dynamo Bleachers are back with a new self-titled album in March and a From The Studio To The Stage Tour that plays MGM Music Hall at Fenway on June 10. Here’s Antonoff checking in : “jack here. we know there’s lots of issues and confusion when buying tickets to shows. want to ensure you we’ve done and will always do everything in our power to make this process as clean and transparent as possible for you all. we’ve had conversations from every single venue and promoter to the heads of the companies to limit fees and advertise only the total price to fans for as many shows as possible. so the ticket price you see is the ticket price you pay. this tour means the world to me and i want to make sure everyone gets in the door feeling right. also keep me posted if you encounter anything weird because i wanna know what you guys deal with and be able to take it right to the top of these companies and do my best to make it easier for bleachers fans and everyone. love you all! see you at FTSTTS ( just wait till you see this shit 🙂 )”.
header: Bleachers , From The Studio To The Stage Tour, June 10

description: Most 20-year-olds walking down Lansdowne Street couldn’t get into some of the bars and clubs along the strip, but The Kid LAROI doesn’t need to worry about any of that. The Australian rapper and singer won’t need ID as he holds court at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on June 16. The artist born Charlton Howard, who popped off after collabs with Juice WRLD and Justin Bieber, announced his The First Time Tour this week, a 31-date run of North America that enlists special guests glaive and Chase Shakur for the Boston show. The tour is named after his 2023 album The First Time , which features appearances from Jungkook, Central Cee, Future, BabyDrill, YoungBoy Never Broke Again, Robert Glasper, and Vanyaland fave D4vd. “I am so beyond excited to see you guys & give you this new show,” he writes on Insta. “It’s been way too long.” Especially in teenage years.
header: The Kid LAROI, The First Time Tour, June 16

description: Welcome back, Lizzy McAlpine . The Berklee grad, who in 2020 kickstarted the school’s #BerkleeAtHome streaming concert series on Instagram, returns to the neighborhood she once called home with two shows at MGM Music Hall at Fenway on June 21 and 22. The Philadelphia native releases new album Older on April 5 via RCA Records, and her third long-player was recorded and produced in Los Angeles by McAlpine and Mason Stoops (Ryan Beatty, Del Water Gap), with additional production by Ryan Lerman of Scary Pockets, Jeremy Most (Emily King, Norah Jones) and Tony Berg (Taylor Swift, Boygenius). Thats quite the lineup. “To me, this album represents who I’ve become over the past three years,” says Lizzy. “Through the long and mostly tumultuous journey of making it, I have learned who I am as a person, who I want to be as an artist and what kind of art I want to make.
header: Lizzy McAlpine , The Older Tour, June 21 and 22

description:
The ’80s were a very long time ago, and yet, pop culture’s greatest decade remains timeless. The music lives on forever as well, as those who made their mark are still out on the road showing off songs that are often older than the crowds that came to hear them. The latest MTV-flavored retro dance party package tour to make the rounds in 2024 is the Totally Tubular Festival , which crashes a new wave down at MGM Music Hall at Fenway on July 17.
The tour features Thomas Dolby (”She Blinded Me With Science”), Tom Bailey of Thompson Twins (”Hold Me Now”), the pictured and embedded Modern English (”I Melt With You”), Men Without Hats (”The Safety Dance”), The Romantics (”What I Like About You”), Bow Wow Wow (”I Want Candy”), Tommy Tutone (“867-5309/Jenny”), and The Plimsouls (”A Million Miles Away”). That’s one hit parade!
“This is a dream lineup for those who love the music of the early 1980s, and for those who want to relive the days…” says Jon Pleeter, of Totally Tubular Festival. “You wore dayglow, you wore parachute pants, you had big hair, perms and more perms, mullets, leg warmers, along with tons of buttons and lots of rubber bracelets. You wore sunglasses at night. The choruses were big, and the hooks were bigger — the party didn’t end.”
header: Totally Tubular Festival , July 17

description: In today’s fast-paced music landscape, Regina Spektor remains timeless. It’s been nearly 25 years since the Moscow-born, Bronx-raised singer-songwriter debuted with 2001’s 11:11 , and now nearly two years — an eternity in the modern age — since her last album Home, before and after . Yet Spektor still commends a crowd like few others, and she returns to Boston on July 31 to play MGM Music Hall at Fenway , part of a short burst of summer shows. “I hope that during these difficult times in the world, you are doing ok, and able to find moments of rest,” she writes on Insta. “I’ve been trying to take better care of myself, and remembering to breathe deep. I hope you have, too. And if not, maybe this little letter is simply a reminder that you can start. Right now… And besides breathing, I’ve also been planning. And the plan involves eight shows this summer in July/August! It will have been a year since my last tour and I can’t wait to see you on the road.” Same, Regina, same.
header: An Evening With Regina Spektor, July 31

description: What the world needs now is a proper blog house resurgence, taking electronic music back to the wild, carefree, pre-EDM neon-punk party days of the late-’00s. And if any project was to deliver us there, it’d be Justice , the French duo who helped define the genre. Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay are prepping Hyperdrama , their first new Justice album in eight years, due out in April, and will then take it across North America, a journey that leads to Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on August 2. After dropping a Tame Impala collab earlier this year, Justice deliver a fresh joint this week called “Saturnine” and featuring Miguel. “We don’t think we’ve ever made anything that sounds remotely like this track before,” Justice state. “It started with Gaspard playing around with an E-mu synthesizer guitar sound, and he found the main riff. The rest came very quickly. We love Miguel’s voice when it’s raw. We wanted him to sound outrageously frontal, with no space around his voice. We felt confident we could make this work with a single mono take of his voice, and minimal processing. It also suited the theme of the song, that’s this sort of fear and loathing in Las Vegas sweaty, hallucinatory flow.
header: Justice: Live, August 2

description: Let’s get “Greedy”! Tate McRae is coming to town, and the rising pop superstar is sticking around for a double-header. The hockey-loving Canadian artist  just announced that her new album Think Later will arrive in December, and she’ll be spending a lot of 2024 on the road supporting it, as two of the 53 dates on the global run include August 9 and 10 romps at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway . “We’re here guys. My sophomore album. This album means sooo much to me and I can’t believe it’s so close to coming out,” McRae writes on Instagram. “Writing this whole thing was one of the most stressful, exciting, nerve racking, and fun things I’ve ever gone through. For the first time in my life I lived this year a little less with my head and a little more with my intuition — and I rlly hope u guys can feel that through the music. Through the biggest highs of my life to the lowest of lows — I feel so happy that it is now gonna be yours <3 Here’s to 20 years old and figuring who the fuck I am haha”.
header: Tate McRae , Think Later Tour, August 9 and 10

description: “Ahhhhhhhhh we get to see you and hold you again???‍” A message like that can come from anyone, but it means something special when it comes from one of three particular sources: A mother, a lover, or The Marías . Luckily for us, that last one checks the box on Insta as the bilingual Los Angeles indie-pop band unveils The Submarine Tour, which snakes its way to Boston for an August 11 party at MGM Music Hall at Fenway . The tour is named for May album submarine , which showcases the psychedelic-soul group’s penchant for genre blending. “ Submarine is an album that represents solitude and exploration,” writes María Zardoya. “We wrote it in the throws of heartbreak, my mind spiraling at each turn, my vision a blur. No one noticed, but there were moments during the writing process where I felt like my mind was underwater and where I couldn’t hear anything except for the echo of my own thoughts. i’ve come out on the other side of that headspace with more clarity than ever and with a project that i’ve never been more proud of. When you’re ready to listen to it, throw some headphones on, find a quiet place where you can be with your inner world and dive in without looking back.” In other words, let it hold you.
header: The Marías, The Submarine Tour, August 11

description:
New Jersey gets shit on so much. Give me seven things that make it great.
Well one, the music. It’s always good. There’s always a good band from New Jersey. Whether it’s Thursday or My Chemical Romance or The Front Bottoms or The Gaslight Anthem or the Bouncing Souls or any band you want to pick. There’s always something coming from New Jersey that’s cool. Like Halsey. Throughout time, Kirsten Dunst was from New Jersey. There’s so many different things. Oh, Scarlett Johansson? You’re welcome. From New Jersey. So, all this stuff. Bleachers? New Jersey. None of those Taylor Swift records would sound like that without New Jersey. What I’m trying to say is, one is always great music, constantly great music.
Two, [the] best pizza in the world is in New Jersey. Everyone can say that it’s from New York – it’s not. It’s been rated. Google dot com. And that’s the end of that. I would say you could also get great pizza… ready for this New York City? In Connecticut. Connecticut has great pizza. Sally’s is good, Frank Pepe’s ? Killer. Nobody cares about Joe’s anymore in New York City. We don’t care. It’s been there for that long. We don’t care. You’ve had enough New York, your time has passed. Now it’s time for Connecticut and New Jersey to shine. That’s what’s up. We might even send some up to Massachusetts. And then what?
Joe’s just opened on Harvard’s campus .
Well, there you go. So, it’s happening. It’s happening already. Spreadin’ the plague, you know what I mean?
Pork roll, that’s third. That’s a reason in and of itself. You better believe it. Pork roll from New Jersey.
Number four. The ocean. The ocean’s great there. You can surf. It’s great. It’s beautiful.
What’s your favorite beach?
Man… I don’t even have one. I don’t care. I’ll just go. I like them all because the one by me is nice in Point Pleasant. The one in Asbury is great. I can’t pick a favorite one.
Number five, I could say that we have some of the most beautiful places in western, like northwestern New Jersey up by Pennsylvania, by the Delaware Water Gap? It’s some of the most beautiful woods and fall scenes that you could find. It’s magical up there. That’s another thing I would recommend about New Jersey.
Number six in New Jersey: Snow. Snow rules. And we get a lot of snow.
And then number seven, why New Jersey is the best? I mean – Bruce Springsteen, that’s why. That’s it. That’s all the reasons you need. That’s everybody’s reasons. So yeah, a great list.

description: From the apartment to the music hall, we’re stoked for a heavy dose of Wallows in 2024. The alt-pop trio, who had one of the defining tracks of the late ’10s when they linked with Clairo for “Are You Bored Yet?” five years ago (!), are back with a new album called Model out in May. A quick summer holiday later, they’re playing Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on August 26, and bringing  pop riser BENEE along for the ride. We got our first taste of the new record this month with the driving “Your Apartment,” a song that just feels like the spring. “We’re so excited and eager to be releasing music for the first time in nearly two years,” Wallows say. “It’s the longest we’ve been silent and it feels good to finally be back.
header: Wallows , Model Tour with BENEE, August 26

description:
From the apartment to the music hall, we’ve been stoked for a continuous dose of Wallows here across 2024. The alt-pop trio, who had one of the defining tracks of the late ’10s when they linked with Clairo for “Are You Bored Yet?” five years ago (!), are back with a new album out this past spring called Model .
A quick summer holiday later, and Wallows are here in town tonight and Tuesday (August 26 and 27), bringing the Model Tour to Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway for a two-nighter with pop riser BENEE coming along for the ride. We got our first taste of the new record way back in March with the driving “Your Apartment,” a song that just feels like it echoes our casual kind of mood.
“We’re so excited and eager to be releasing music for the first time in nearly two years,” Wallows say. “It’s the longest we’ve been silent and it feels good to finally be back. This is the first song from our new album that fully came together lyrically quite some time ago now, so it feels right that it gets heard first.”
header: WALLOWS + BENEE :: Monday, August 26 and Tuesday, August 27 at MGM Music Hall at Fenway, 2 Lansdowne St. in Boston, MA :: 6:40 p.m., all ages, $34.50 to $79.50 :: Event info and tickets

description: We often talk about enduring bands as rock and roll survivalists, skillfully weathering trends and scenes to stay relevant as their contemporaries fade away to time. If there is a parallel scope for electronic music, then Porter Robinson is right there near the top, as the Atlanta-born DJ, record producer, and singer-songwriter has remained in-demand and notable long after the EDM craze wore off with last night’s pills. With new third album SMILE! set for release in July via Mom+Pop, Robinson has unveiled his “first-ever” world tour, and the SMILE! 😀 run (yeah, that’s what it’s called) kicks off its North American leg with a pair of summer’s-over parties at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on August 29 and 30.
header: Porter Robinson , SMILE! 😀 World Tour, August 29 and 30

description: It’s the most wonderful time of the year. No, silly Goose , we’re not talking about Christmas — we’re talking about Goosemas, the Connecticut jam band’s annual holiday soiree that puts a big fat bow on the year that was. The road that leads to this year’s Goosemas, held down in South Carolina in December (obviously), begins here on Lansdowne Street, as Goose hold court at MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston over three nights, September 2, 3, and 4. Things get started on Labor Day and extend the holiday weekend vibes well into the workweek, as the tireless live band delivers one sterling indie groove to keep us warm and fuzzed out. We’re firm believers that the autumn season begins that first weekend of September, so this is a solid way to head towards the best time of the year.
header: Goose , An Evening with Goose, September 2, 3, and 4

description: And now we kneel at the altar of St. Vincent . The era-defining project of a certain Annie Clark — certainly no stranger to our extensive digital pages — is back with new album All Born Screaming , set for release later this month, and a tour that takes her to Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on September 5. Joining her this show will be Yves Tumor. We’ve already received a few tastes of the new record, and it’s shaping up to be one we’ll all be reading about again in December; it boasts an all-star lineup of guests, including Cate Le Bon, Josh Freese, Stella Mozgawa, Rachel Eckroth, Mark Guiliana, and David Ralicke. Around the tour news, St. Vincent dropped the pulsating “Flea,” featuring Dave Grohl on drums and Justin Meldal-Johnsen on bass. Not a bad look.
header: St. Vincent , All Born Screaming Tour, September 5

description: Alan Walker is a global phenomenon. The enduring Norwegian DJ and producer has been jet-setting around the world for a few busy years now, and brings his energetic and affirming dance party to MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston on September 14, part of a short run of North American dates tucked between massive appearances across Europe, India, and pretty much everywhere else. Since he arrived on the scene in 2015 as a teenager with debut banger “Faded,” now creeping up on two billion streams on Spotify and 3.7 billion views on YouTube, Walker and his rabid fanbase of Walkers have been doing the impossible: Keeping EDM fresh and vibrant long after the trendy kids moved on to other things. The hooded n’ masked artist has collaborated with the likes of Ava Max, Hans Zimmer, Noah Cyrus, Sia, Bruno Mars, Coldplay, and others, and now brings his insane visuals and dazzling production to Lansdowne.
header: Alan Walker , September 14

description: With all the distracted talk of “happy hour” returning to Massachusetts, Kehlani is busy out here delivering the late-night “After Hours” vibes we really need. The Bay Area R&B artist brings her Crash World tour to Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on September 17, with FLO and Anycia on board, riding high on their new album of the same name and thumping May single, which scored Kehlani a Top 5 hit on Billboard’s Rhythmic Airplay chart. June’s Crash , which features Jill Scott, Young Miko and Omah Lay, did even better; peaking at Number 2 on Billboard’s Top R&B albums chart. “For a long time, I’ve been not afraid of how I’ve been perceived musically, but I had a lot of being very apologetic in my personhood, for who I am, for anything I’ve done, for anything I had to be corrected on for any way I’ve shown up in the world,” Kehlani tells Essence . “In this album specifically, I am just gonna talk and not hold back. I’m going to talk as if I was talking to my very best friend.” That’s us. We’re all the BFF.
header: Kehlani , Crash World Tour, September 17

description: The fall concert calendar has a new holiday entry, as PJ Harvey is set to return to Boston for the artist’s first North American tour in seven years. An Evening With PJ Harvey, as it’s perfectly billed, lands at MGM Music Hall at Fenway on September 18, in support of last summer’s I Inside the Old Year Dying album. And with the tour announcement comes a new video for the record’s “Seem an I,” directed by Colm Bairéad and starring actor Ruth Wilson. Harvey has this to say about it: “Ruth and I became friends after working together on Clio Barnard’s film Dark River . I have always greatly admired Ruth’s work as an actor, so had long harbored a dream that we might work together again in some way. When the opportunity to work with Colm Bairéad came up I knew him to be a director Ruth thought highly of, as I did, so it felt right to ask her if she would star in the film.
header: An Evening With PJ Harvey , September 18

description: Hey now, hey now now — The Sisters of Mercy are coming back to North America. That’s news in and of itself, as the influential British don’t-dare-call-us-goth collective led by Andrew Eldritch returned to our shores last year for the first time in 14 years, and now demand “More” by way of a 26-date fall run that includes a September 22 gathering at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway . Though The Sisters of Mercy have not released an album since 1990’s Vision Thing (which is kind of crazy), they remain a fixture across dark disco and underground dance floors, and the sonic arsenal these days plays like a never-ending greatest hits assault: “Temple of Love,” “Dominion,” “Marian,” “Lucretia My Reflection,” “This Corrosion,” and all the other songs that echo off a punk-psychedelia strobe light. They still sound as lethal as they did decades ago, when we all first heard them and pivoted our collective tastes into something a little more sinister. As an added treat, AFI side project Blaqk Audio opens the show.
header: The Sisters of Mercy, September 22

description: Earlier this week we broke the news of Queens of the Stone Age’s upcoming mini-tour, which kicks off at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on September 28. Vanyaland got on the horn with QOTSA keyboardist/guitarist Dean Fertita for the exclusive scoop on the dates , with The Kills on board, the latest in support of desert rock icons album In Times New Roman… and final shows on their ongoing The End is Nero Tour. “We’re comin’ to Boston to start a few weeks in the States,” he says. “Boston will be the first and that was the second show of this entire tour for the record, so it’ll be nice to do a proper Boston show.” Fertita added that the band is able to flex its catalog muscle a bit with these headlining gigs, as ooposed to festival appearances: “I don’t want to say we’ve never thought about or cared about that too much, because we always just wanted to play our show – no matter what. But I think we’ve been experimenting with that a little bit when we do these festival shows and sort of knowing what people want to hear and what they’re there for and they’ve been standing outside all day, so you kinda are aware when you are writing a set. When we do our own shows, and we know that people have been with us from the start, we can kind of get into some deeper album cuts.
header: Queens of the Stone Age , The End is Nero, September 28

description: Where were you in 1998? Probably vibing along to Air’s Moon Safari , allowing the brain to melt over electronic music in a way it may never have before, and feeling cooler than literally anyone else around you as the beats and treats filled the headphones of your Sony CD Discman. This fall, the French duo of Nicolas Godin and Jean-Benoît Dunckel take their classic debut album out on the North American road for some 25th anniversary affection, seducing Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on October 15. It’s the first time Air will perform the record in full on this continent, according to reports, and the show will be augmented by other faves from their catalog and the usual Air visual experience. Moon Safari also gets the anniversary deluxe edition reissue treatment this month, featuring rarities, demos, videos, BBC sessions, and a Blu-ray version of the album containing a Dolby Atmos mix. We didn’t appreciate the simplicity of the late-’90s as they were happening, so this is a nice time machine back to better days.
header: Air, Air Play Moon Safari, October 15

description: Are you gonna match her freak? That’s what Tinashe wants to know, as the viral R&B star unveils her Match My Freak World Tour that plays Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on November 6. It’s been a whirlwind summer for the Kentucky-born, California-raised singer, writer, and dancer, as chart-topping single “Nasty” — hitting Number 1 on Spotify’s Global Viral 50 and US Viral 50 charts, and Apple iTunes R&B and Soul Songs chart — delivered her biggest track in a decade, with the lyrical hook “Is somebody gonna match my freak?” taking on its own life on the internet. “I want people to know that you can steer your own ship, create your own destiny, and mold your own universe,”  says Tinashe. “That’s especially important for young women. I’m working towards constant evolution, growth, journey, and adventure. I’m embracing it for what it is, living life to the fullest, and taking advantage of being able to do what I love. I’m living my dream.” Tinashe’s new album, Quantum Baby , hits this month, as well.
header: Tinashe , Match My Freak World Tour, November 6

description: It’s probably time for a discussion on the greatest songwriters and lyricists of the 21st century, and in that discussion is Isaac Brock of Modest Mouse . And no better way to showcase a particular strength than revisiting the Portland indie icons’ breakthrough 2004 album Good News For People Who Love Bad News , which after a Legacy Recordings expanded edition release earlier this year gets the 20th anniversary tour treatment this fall. Included in the run is a stop at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on November 19 with The Black Heart Procession. With era-defining tracks like “Float On,” “The World At Large,” and “Ocean Breathes Salty,” the record went certified double platinum here in the states, moving two million units, and helped elevate the band from underground heroes to mainstream success story. It set a tone for the two decades that followed. “‘Float On’ wasn’t really written until the last couple of days of tracking,” Brock tells Rolling Stone . “Once it got done, I was like, ‘Yeah, this is fun.’ I mean, lyrically, I kind of felt like maybe it was a bit too goofy, and shit. Like, ‘This is fun, but is it silly?’.” History will be the judge.
header: Modest Mouse , Good News For People Who Love Bad News Anniversary Tour, November 19

description: Sturgill Simpson is a man of his word. After promising to release only five studio albums under his own name, the famed Kentucky-born country artist kickstarts a new era as Johnny Blue Skies with the release of Passage Du Desir on July 12 via his own independent label High Top Mountain Records. With the new music comes new live shows, and Simpson closes out his first tour in four years with two appearances at MGM Music Hall at Fenway , this November 23 and 24. The run is dubbed the Why Not? Tour, and Simpson has a plan to ease the burden of high ticket prices. “The ‘Why Not?’ tour has opted out of using dynamic ticket pricing,” reads a video statement, viewable below. “We will be doing everything in our power to keep tickets in the hands of fans and out of the hands of scalpers.
header: Sturgill Simpson , An Evening with Sturgill Simpson – Why Not? Tour, November 23 and 24 (second show added)

description: It’s only fitting that as the northern lights stretched high across Northeastern skies, AURORA has unveiled her North American tour. The Norwegian electronic-pop songwriter and producer brings her ethereal sounds to Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on December 4, helping close out a year that delivers new album What Happened To The Heart? in June. The Glassnote Records, Decca Records, and Petroleum release has been augmented by  a string of singles, including the glowing “Some Type of Skin,” which can be heard below. AURORA declares this new album her “most personal and cathartic album” to date, adding: “Though its precise function and anatomy were not clearly understood, the heart was believed to be the centre of the soul. Of intuition. Of emotion and intention. Until we decided these were qualifications of the mind. Emotion overpowered by logic. And with the world being so corrupted by money, power and selfishness you cannot help but ask yourself – what happened to the heart?” We’ll find out soon enough.
header: AURORA, What Happened To The Earth? Part 2 Tour, December 4

description: It’s a new Boston music tradition, like the Dropkicks on St. Patrick’s Day or the Mighty Mighty Bosstones over the holidays — only here, the rooms keep getting bigger. The Elovaters have announced another January show to heat up the hometown masses with warm vibes in the coldest month, and this year’s celebration goes down January 18 at MGM Music Hall at Fenway . It continues an impressive winter rise for the Boston progressive roots and reggae rock brigade that began in the clubs and elevated from the ‘Dise to House of Blues and now MGM, and this gig welcomes V faves Moon Taxi as direct support. The Elovaters were named Live Artist of the Year and Reggae/Ska Artist of the Year at the 2023 Boston Music Awards , and last year’s global breakout album Endless Summer has plenty of juice left, taking the band across festival appearances at Cali Vibes, California Roots, Levitate Backyard, and Rise and Vibes Music Festival. The Roll Up fall tour of North America kicks off today, coincidentally enough, before taking the dudes to Australia and New Zealand in November. Come January, Lansdowne will be once again transformed with post-holiday cheer no matter what the weather may bring. Get loose with new single “Red Wine” below.
header: The Elovaters, January 18

description: Word on the street is that Hippo Campus have crafted “the best album they have ever made,” and that comes right from the Minnesota indie rock band’s HQ. We’ll soon get to test that claim, as the Twin Cities luminaries, never short on confidence, release FLOOD on September 20. They’ll soon take it out for an extensive 2025 North American tour, hitting more than 30 cities, including a stop at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on February 7. We got a taste of the new material over the summer with the glistening “Paranoid,” and Hippo Campus set it all up for us with the following: “‘Paranoid’ is the collection of sun flares plastered against your eyelids after falling asleep outside,” they declare. “What’s left of whipping shitties in your self-conscious for too long. It’s a hard look in the unforgiving mirror and the sobering realization that not all questions have answers.” Oh, we feel that.
header: Hippo Campus , FLOOD Tour, February 7

description: In a recent interview with Zane Lowe, the dude FINNEAS revealed it took him only 14 days to craft his new album For Cryin’ Out Loud . Now, the songwriter, producer, and big brother collaborator to Billie Eilish is taking the record out for 14 shows across North America in the New Year. Coincidence? Hey, maybe! Included in that run is a February 21 twirl at MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston, and he’s bringing Bad Suns along for the ride. “I had the honor of making these songs with some of my closest friends and I can’t wait for them to be yours,” the artist born Finneas Baird O’Connell says on Insta. We’ve long hyped the alt-pop stylings of Billie Eilish, dating back to her “Six Feet Under” demo way back in ’16 , and it’s been wild to see the rise of the brother/sister duo. Family first. Check out the For Cryin’ Out Loud album closer “Lotus Eater” below.

description: There age of the rock and roll star is long dead, but there remains an unmistakable aura around Father John Misty . The man his family calls Joshua Michael Tillman has a new album called Mahashmashana due out just before Thanksgiving, and after a little holiday break takes he it out on the road for a North American tour that plays MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston on February 22. And he’s got Destroyer in tow, so it’ll be worth battling the snow on Lansdowne Street to get in early. Mahashmashana , meanwhile, is the Mist’s sixth studio album, produced by himself and Drew Erickson, and its Sanskrit title translates to “great cremation ground, all things going thither.” The dude still has us learning things after all these years. A few tracks have already been released from the eight-song record, and we invite everyone to go from Vanyaland to “Screamland” below.
header: Father John Misty, February 22

description: Anyone who reads Vanyaland on the regular knows that we routinely roll out two types of live music announcements: Band in the USA for tour unveilings and Fest Intentions for festival lineup reveals. But damned if we were not too sure how to slot Movements ‘ just-announced 2025 North American run, because while its pretty much a standard tour of the country, bringing along Citizen, Scowl, and Downward certainly gives it an eye-catching and ear-splitting festival vibe. The tour rolls into Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on March 13. Movements, the Orange County post-hardcore band that dropped third album Ruckus! last year, lead a spectrum of heavy sounds heard each night that range from hardcore to indie to shoegaze, and followed up the album this summer with shimmering new single “Afraid to Die.” Says vocalist Patrick Miranda: “With “Afraid to Die,’ we were able to take the energy that was in RUCKUS! and fine-tune it by exploring different realms of what this band can be and what our music can sound like, and I think we did a good job… Sonically, it’s so different than anything we’ve ever done, and yet I think it still pulls on the heartstrings as a lot of our older music does.
header: Movements , March 13

description: We’re about halfway to St. Patrick’s Day, which means it’s time to start planning our March festivities with the Dropkick Murphys . The Boston punk band unveiled dates and details for their 2025 St. Patrick’s Day Celebration, and it kicks off with a March to 16 swing at MGM Music Hall at Fenway before a March 17 throwdown at the House of Blues. Joining Ken Casey and the boys at MGM will be The Menzingers, Bouncing Souls, Hot Water Music, and more. And to get us worked up, the Dropkicks just unveiled a new video for “Sirens,” the first hint of a new album to arrive in ’25. Says Casey about the punchy track: “For nearly a decade, the division between red and blue, right and left, has grown deeper, darker and uglier — dividing families, and ending friendships. Nobody enjoys this more than the billionaires, who are making record profits off the blood, sweat, and tears of the working class. They love it when we fight amongst ourselves, because their biggest fear is us joining together to come after them… THE REAL ENEMY.” We’re about to run through the wall.
header: Dropkick Murphys, St. Patrick’s Day Celebration, March 14 to 16

description:
We love a good flex. So we couldn’t help but notice that when Nathaniel Rateliff & The Night Sweats ‘ label team of Stax/Fantasy/Concord sent out a quick press release last month for new single “Call Me (Whatever You Like)”, it included some streaming links, a press photo, tour dates, and four select pull quotes. Those quotes didn’t come from press, radio, or blogs, they came from Howard Stern, Noah Kahan, Zach Bryan, and Robert Plant. That’s some heavy-hitter action. The spotlight track is the follow-up to previous single “Heartless,” listenable below, and both are included on the Americana band’s summer album South Of Here . Now Rateliff and the dudes have announced an extended run of tour dates for the record, and it wraps with a March 28 gig at MGM Music Hall at Fenway in Boston. “We have dreamt of playing shows like this for our entire career, to know they are actually happening feels bigger than any dream I could have had,” Rateliff says . “This tour wouldn’t be possible without you all, I feel your love so deeply. Thank you for your endless support, see you soon.” Now that’s a quote.

description: There’s a force brewing from the north, and it descends on our unsuspecting city in the spring. Spiritbox , the two-time Grammy-nominated progressive metal band from British Columbia, have outlined a powerful North American tour package that crashes Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on April 19, bringing Loathe, Dying Wish, and GEL along for what promises to be a very loud ride. Spiritbox are hitting the road in support of their highly anticipated sophomore album Tsunami Sea , which hits March 7 via Pale Chord/Rise Records. The tour news comes after Spiritbox were nominated for a second Grammy in the Best Metal Performance category, for “Cellar Door” off last year’s The Fear of Fear EP. The band writes on Insta: “Thank you to the @recordingacademy for our nomination in the best metal performance category for ‘Cellar Door’. We are so honored to be nominated two years in a row off the same EP and to be amongst all these incredible nominees.” Give it a spin below.
header: Spiritbox , Tsunami Sea North American Tour, April 19

description:
It seems like only yesterday we were interviewing Lucy Dacus at Boston Calling, but so much has happened in the near-decade since. The Virginia-born singer-songwriter, guitarist, record producer, and boygenius member has become one of the most beloved voices in indie and folk, and now preps her fourth studio album, Forever Is A Feeling , due out March 28 via Geffen Records. “I got kicked in the head with emotions,” Dacus says about it. “Falling in love, falling out of love.” A North American tour aligns with the record, and Dacus brings her delicate new tunes to Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway for a pair of shows on April 20 and 21, with Katie Gavin and jasmine.4.t solidifying the evenings’ mood. Forever Is A Feeling welcomes an immense roster of guest talent, including Hozier, fellow boygenius collaborators Phoebe Bridgers and Julien Baker, as well as Blake Mills, Bartees Strange, Madison Cunningham, Collin Pastore, and others — and it makes sense because when Dacus calls, everyone answers. Check out new single “Ankles,” which debuted on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , and embrace the melancholy.

description: There is a healthy list of anticipated albums soon arriving in 2025, and near the top of the list is the latest from Japanese Breakfast . The celebrated project of musician, singer, songwriter, and author Michelle Zauner releases For Melancholy Brunettes (& sad women) in March via Dead Oceans, and quickly follows with a North American tour that plays Coachella Music and Arts Festival and ACL Live before appearing at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on May 7. According to the album announcement, the 10-track effort, led by new single “Orlando In Love,” is said to explore “the darker waves that roil within, the moody, fecund field of melancholy, long held to be the psychic state of poets on the verge of inspiration.
header: Japanese Breakfast, The Melancholy Tour, May 7

description: It’s absolutely wild that it’s been nearly 20 years since Empire of the Sun first crashed our hearts, minds, and iPods with Walking on a Dream , the cinematic Australian electronic duo’s 2008 debut album that still sounds like the future. Led by the billion-streaming title track, the record instantly made icons of Luke Steele and Nick Littlemore, and the duo have kept a steady beat ever since. Over the summer they dropped new album Ask That God , and now a North American tour of the same name sets sail in the spring, highlighted by a May 24 show at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway . “This body of work represents the greatest shift in consciousness our world has ever seen and that’s reflected in the music,” says Littlemore . Adds Steele: “We are nothing more than conduits, gathering experience and finding what is meant for the Empire to find.
header: Empire of the Sun , Ask That God Tour, May 24

description: What a time to be young and alive in Boston during the winter of 2025: The Red Sox were World Series champions, Vice magazine was essential reading, and the indie dance party ruled the rock clubs. And an exciting new English band called Bloc Party soundtracked it all with an iconic and incendiary debut album in Silent Alarm , a rhythm section-fueled mammoth album of emotion filled with essential aughts bangers like “Banquet,” “This Modern Love,” and “Helicopter.” Two decades quickly followed, and we’re still chasing that high. Now Bloc Party bring the record and all its jagged beauty back to North America for a very attractive May 30 dance party at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway , the first of 13 continental dates after Kele and the gang play SoCal’s Just Like Heaven festival. Joining the fun are Canadian alt-rock radio faves Metric, who show off their 2009 album Fantasies , itself filled with indie bangers like “Help I’m Alive,” “Gold Guns Girls,” and “Gimme Sympathy.” This will be the family reunion we’ve all been waiting for.
header: Bloc Party , 20 Years Of Bloc Party: Silent Alarm & Greatest Hits, May 30

description:
The latest Kills record is called God Games . Give me seven of your favorite games. This could be anything that qualifies as a game: board game, drinking game… it could be a game you play on your cellphone if you do that.
Hince: Well, I mean there’s a game that used to be a massive part of our lives, and it was called Kariki, and it is a dice game. We don’t play that so much anymore because it’s not a popular thing. Whenever you play it with someone, you’ve got to explain the rules so it gets slightly [monotonous]. It becomes a kind of gang thing that when you’re with people that know how to play, is amazing. Cury
Mosshart: Rummikub is my favorite game.
Hince: I won’t even say the word, let alone play the game or learn the rules.
Mosshart [laughing]: So much fun.
Hince: Gin Rummy I’m going for, because it’s a game that I play almost absolutely every week, but almost two or three times a week with my friend. Yeah, there’s this new gang of weird people that are really into playing cards, and we’ll go out to bars and just play cards.
Hince: Can we say Formula One Grand Prix? It’s a game – kind of game.
Mosshart: That’s my ultimate favorite game.
Mosshart: It’s a racing game.
Hince: It’s an absolute passion, to be honest.
Mosshart: I like backgammon. Classic game.
Hince: I like the Rizla game. Whatever you call that, everyone has a different name for it [Forehead Detective]. We call it the Rizla game because, you know, cigarette papers. You write someone’s name on it and stick it on your head, and you have to [figure out the name]. That gets played quite a lot.
Mosshart: I like Spelling Bee. Every day I play Spelling Bee.
Hince: Alright. Now I’ve thought, because I do all these…
Mosshart: Wordle and Strands…
Hince: I do all these geography games every day. I do like to sort of test my knowledge of geography. But yeah…
Mosshart: You can take away my backgammon and do that one.
Hince: I don’t like backgammon. It’s such a [pointless] game.
Mosshart: You can change it to this one because it’s pretty amazing.
Hince: I refuse to learn the rules of backgammon.
Mosshart: I’ve just given you a free game. So, explain your geography game [laughs].
Hince: Okay. It’s a geography game, it’s called Worldle . Not Wordle – I know what you’re going to say. Worldle . And you just get the outline of a country, like the silhouette of a country, and you have to guess where it is. So, you just guess the country, and then it’ll say, “No, you are 3000 miles in the wrong direction.” And you have to pinpoint it from there. And I’ve got pretty damn good at it. I normally get it within three.
Mosshart: You’re also very good at guessing flags.
Hince: I’m getting better at flags. Favorite flag? Zambia .
Wow. I don’t think I’ve ever met someone who had a favorite flag that was Zambia.
Hince: Oh my god. Zambia. It’s like, it looks like a sort of Stanley Kubrick set against the green screen. It’s like got an eagle on this black, golden, red sort of plinth thing. And then it’s green in the background, like a green screen. It’s really odd. And the other flag would be the Saudi Arabian flag because it’s the only flag that is, it’s different on both sides of the flag. Do you know what I mean?
Mosshart: Oh, it’s two sides.
Hince: Yeah. But because it’s got, right, every flag has two sides, but most of the time it’s just the reverse. But this is actually different because it’s writing, so on the other side, if they mirrored it, it would be backwards. So, they’ve done it, and it’s the only flag that does that.

description: Here’s a new motto we are taking into 2025: Long Hair, Long Life. And it’s not just a vibe to help us get through some crazy times, it’s also the name of a co-headline tour from Peach Pit and Briston Maroney , who team up for 25 dates in the spring across an unsuspecting North America. Along the way is a June 24 stop at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway , and by then we’ll likely know all the words to Peach Pit’s recent album Magpie , which should enjoy a shelf life well into next year. “We couldn’t be more excited for this upcoming tour with our good friend Briston Maroney,” says Peach Pit vocalist Neil Smith. “It’s our biggest tour ever and we’re playing some really crazy venues, places like Red Rocks in Colorado that I honestly never really thought were in the cards for us. It freaks me out that we somehow managed to go from rehearsing in Chris’ bedroom 10 years ago to venues like The Greek in LA and Pier 17 in New York. 2014 Peach Pit would be tripping out right now.” Heck, we’re tripping out right now.
header: Peach Pit & Briston Maroney , Long Hair, Long Life Tour, June 24

description: The upcoming 2025 is destined to be the Year of Pixies . Which is wild, because for us here in Massachusetts, every year since like 1988 has been the Year of Pixies. But the iconic and influential indie band delivered a new album called The Night the Zombies Came last week, just in time for a proper Halloween scream, and will set off on a tour next summer that delivers them to Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway for two nights on July 18 and 19. Each evening will have its own flair: Night one sees Pixies performing fan-favorite albums Bossanova and Trompe le Monde in full; while night two promises a mix of classics from across their storied and often-imitated catalog, including songs from the new record. It should be a special homecoming doubleheader. The Night the Zombies Came is the band’s 10th overall — if counting their classic 1987 4AD mini LP Come On Pilgrim , as suggested by pixiesmerch.com — and first dose of new music since 2022’s Doggerel . It was recorded at Vermont’s Guilford Sound studios with producer Tom Dalgety, and features new bassist Emma Richardson. Check out our recent article on the band giving reunion advice to Oasis , and hear new single “The Vegas Suite” below.
header: Pixies , July 18 and 19

description: Lord Huron are about to set off on their biggest headline tour of North America yet — and that’s not what generated the most headlines this week. The Los Angeles indie-folk band, which plays Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on August 3 with Lee Fields as direct support, released cinematic new single “Who Laughs Last?”, and both the track and the video stars Academy Award-nominated actor Kristen Stewart . That’s a solid get! It’s the Love Lies Bleeding luminary’s debut recording, and here’s what she has to say about it: “I’ve always loved the band and immediately sparked to the manic drift of the song and to the mood. I love when a song is something you can kind of seep into and imagine. Ben [Schneider, frontman] is the nicest, I was so into reading his words… there’s nothing like making new friends through projects like these that just crop up. Lucky stuff.” Maybe we’ll get a cameo at MGM in the summer; Boston is “Hollywood East,” after all.

description: There’s nothing quite like those last few days of summer, when we come together to reminisce over the carefree days of yesterday and sing the songs of our youth with those we love the most. Coheed and Cambria are providing an especially inspired opportunity, as the New York progressive rock band teams up with emo veterans Taking Back Sunday for a co-headlining tour that plays Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway on August 30. And they’re bringing Foxing along for the ride. The nostalgia is met with some modern flair, as Coheed just dropped an upbeat new track called “Someone Who Can,” from forthcoming album The Father of Make Believe , and it ties in nicely with how we’ll be feeling on Lansdowne Street that night. “When you’re growing up, you’re perpetually trying to understand the world that’s changing around you,” says Claudio Sanchez. “Over time, it’s comforting to reach the conclusion that you’ll never truly have things figured out.”  Check out the video, directed by Mason Mercer, below.

description: This miserable year so far hasn’t given us much to be excited about, but suddenly we have a new reason to stay relatively sane through the chaos: Rilo Kiley are back. The influential Los Angeles indie band led by Jenny Lewis and Blake Sennett play their first live shows since 2008 this year, and included in the late-summer run is a September 7 party at Boston’s MGM Music Hall at Fenway . And that means we all have a chance to hear, to sing, and to love “Portions For Foxes,” one of the most iconic and undeniable songs of the 21st century. And a greatest hits album, titled That’s How We Choose To Remember It , arrives in May via Saddle Creek. “It couldn’t have happened any sooner,” Lewis says. “It feels like now is the time to share that joy and love with each other and with everyone else.” And Sennett adds: “For some people, Rilo Kiley evokes a formative, emotional time in life, when you were maybe grasping for your place in the universe. We were too.” Revisit the timeless beauty that is “Portions for Foxes” — which somehow is 21 years old now?!?! — and prepare for the aughts kid family reunion in September.

description:
Give me seven dream dinner guests whom you’d like to cook for; they can be alive or dead.
Wow. Okay. Let’s go with the people that aren’t around, I suppose, because then it’s kind of awkward, because if I mention anyone’s famous, the chances are I’m going to be trying to find them to be on the show. [laughs] So I don’t want to preempt it.
I did a great book podcast recently, and they asked me to be talking about one of my favorite books that sort of shaped me. And it was The New York Trilogy , Paul Auster , which is this book [holds up a worn paperback copy]. I’ve been rereading it. I realized that it came at this incredible time in my life, where the protagonist in this book is going through a lot of loss, and change, and identity. And it’s a very, very moving book. And I hadn’t realized how… This is when I was still on government welfare and painting and decorating and rehearsing in the evenings and living a life of real, a true working musician, like a working man, working kid. So, Paul Auster, he recently passed away and it struck me, like, because I always have these plans of reaching out to certain people that have inspired me, and I don’t know how I never reached out to him. I’ve read more or less everything he’s ever written, and he was a well-known figure in Brooklyn. And so, Paul Auster would be the first guest that I’d be really interested in.
Who would be fascinating? I think Marilyn Monroe . Well, because I feel the society was just sort of… It was a very, very tough time then to be a strong woman. And so, I would find her fascinating. What was she really like? Where was she at? I think that would be really incredible.
I think that David Bowie , because I just would like to have him back, and if my dinner’s the excuse to bring him back to us, momentarily, that’d be wonderful. He’s a great man and so interesting. So he would be one.
There’d be probably the painter, Francis Bacon , because he’s my favorite painter. So you got my favorite author, favorite painter, favorite musician, Francis Bacon, because he just… I’ve read these books when there’s this guy, David Sylvester, who does interviews with him . And it’s just so fun hearing people talk about art, who are amazing artists, and just the rules and what works, what doesn’t work, why things are great. “Champagne for my real friends, real pain for my sham friends.” He would be great.
My mum then. I would love my mum. It’s like… I had a very torturous life with her. In fact, it’s funny because in the [Paul Auster] book, which I hadn’t mentioned, his mother dies, gets hit by bus when he’s 13. And my mum left our house, went to move to a different country – I didn’t live with her ever again – when I was 12. So that sort of seismic kind of like… I mean, I have a 12-year-old son now I don’t like being away from. We obviously were in contact, and when she came back to England a couple years later, I would see her once a year, but we really, really connected when I was 27. We started to get much closer again, and we’d see her more. And because she’s my mum, I totally forgave her. I love her. I adored her. And I just took it as, like, I didn’t take it personally. I took it like she just wanted a better life and didn’t think the life was with us. And that was a wild lesson because it wasn’t in the years of therapy or anyone’s help. You just would be crippled on the inside. And I didn’t take it as anything to do with my fault. I took it as, like, adults have problems and are fucked up too. That’s how I felt it. Because I knew that she loved me, but it must have been a lot for her to be away from me, and she must have had her reasons.
So as she was going through the dying process, I really hoped… I’ve heard that some people go for complete closure and they investigate everything. Other people just do not. And my mum was so worried about dying, that we never had discussions about her dying because it was always about getting her better. Even though it was obvious she was dying, the vernacular was always about, “let’s get you better, got to get you strong.” I spent the last five weeks, and I cooked for her every day. I didn’t want to hassle her in her house. She lived like 40 minutes from me in London, about an hour for me. So, every day I would cook at my house. I’d do, like, Meals on Wheels. I would package it all up, really useful stuff, beautifully packaged. It was really nice. Everything I cooked went into clean, brand-new pots. And so it would arrive like a sort of bespoke lunch.
I’d go and sit with her for 10 minutes and have lunch with her. And then I’d talk to her for 20 minutes, half an hour. And then people who are not well, they don’t want people around a lot. Her husband was there. So, I would leave. It was exhausting, but it was wild. And I hoped there was some closure there, but she wasn’t into that. She wasn’t into that. But I wouldn’t have her around to recriminate her. I forgave her a long time ago. I just would be intrigued, like whether she felt she got what she wanted. She didn’t. She sort of bounced around and three stepfathers and all that sort of stuff. And so one didn’t really work out for her. It was really sad. But yeah, so my mum would be an amazing guest.
Well, I mean, I have to have my dad because I can’t have my mum… and I grew up with my dad. So my dad was the really, really solid one. So he were there, but we’re losing your viewers now because no one cares if I have lived with my dad [laughs], but I really love that. My dad.
And on a final note, this Rob Reiner was a really terrible, tragic situation. Mental illness. I mean, I have heard that no one has been to see [Reiner’s son Nick, who is charged with the murder]. I read in the paper . Gosh, just so unwell. The thing was that I’ve dealt with a few people in my life with schizophrenia, and I don’t quite know what he would be suffering from, obviously some psychosis as well, but what a great man, what a great director, what a funny man, and brought so much joy to so many people. And you know that he was obviously struggling with his son and did everything for him and tried to support him through all of his trials and tribulations.
And then this tragic, like horrific ending to their lives, just makes me think of him. I started thinking of people who were gone, and that was just a terrible situation. So he’d be an amazing dinner guest for all the good things and all the good times and all the things.
